title: Teddy Wilson's record date featuring Boots Castle
summary: Teddy Wilson cuts a Kansas City date with Harry James, Gene Krupa and Harry Goodman, featuring Boots singing 'The Hour of Parting'; Leeman was not on it.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I used to go out and hang out with MaryLou Williams, and Boots used to -- Boots was a great singer, by the way, and about that Fall, Benny Goodman came by there at the theatre, and Teddy Wilson had his own record date, and then ...
In Kansas City?
* Dick Wilson.
Yes.
: But what year was this?
He had a record date in Kansas City.
: When was this? 1935, wasn't it?
Do you remember if Teddy played on that date? Did you do it with him?
Yes. Teddy took some of the guys from Benny's band, because they were there, and there was Harry James on trumpet, Gene Krupa on drums, and Teddy Wilson.
: This is 1935, huh?
Yes, Teddy Wilson's orchestra. And it featured Boots Castle, and who else was on that -- I think Harry Goodman was on base.
: Oh yeah, Harry was Benny's brother.
And I know one of the songs she sang, 'The Hour of Parting' -- it was a double -- a single record, double size.
: This is before Teddy joined Benny?
No, he's with Benny.
: Oh, he's with Benny now.
Yeah. I might be a month off, it might have been January of '36.
: Oh now, I couldn't dispute that.
He made the record, because I have it at home.
And you made the record, you were on the record?
No, I didn't make the record.
Oh, I see.
She made the record. This is Boots.
Oh, Boots.
And she sang beautifully.
Oh, I see.
